card: Ensures port numbers are formatted as four zero-padded hex characters in the feature_anchors functional test. Running the test suite with custom low port numbers (such as TEST_RUNNER_PORT_MIN=1100) previously failed an assertion against serialized anchor data because ports under 4096 formatted to only three hex characters. The PR description provides a reproducible command demonstrating the test failure on master.
evidence: PR description demonstrates exact failure reproduction: running `TEST_RUNNER_PORT_MIN=1100 test/functional/feature_anchors.py` fails on master at `assert ip_port in anchors_hex`
problem: Running `feature_anchors.py` with port numbers below 4096 (such as with `TEST_RUNNER_PORT_MIN=1100`) fails with an `AssertionError`. The test formats the two-byte port using `hex(port)[2:]`, producing a three-digit hex string instead of the four-digit serialized representation.

risk.why: A mistake would only cause the feature_anchors functional test to falsely pass or fail.

summary: Fixes port hex-formatting in the `feature_anchors.py` functional test to always zero-pad to four hex characters. When running functional tests with a lower custom port range, the unpadded port string caused an assertion failure against the serialized binary anchor data.
